safe.title: DI recovery
safe.decision_note: The committed effect is recovered from authoritative state. A second mutation is blocked.
safe.explanation: Authoritative evidence found the committed effect, so a second mutation is not permitted.

steps.title: Submit one intended payment
steps.detail: The request is bound to one logical operation and one stable effect identity.

steps.title: The financial effect exists
steps.detail: The deterministic sandbox stores exactly one committed effect.

steps.title: The acknowledgement is lost
steps.detail: The client cannot infer commit outcome from a missing transport response.

steps.title: Recover authoritative state
steps.detail: Lookup finds the existing committed effect under the preserved identity.

steps.title: Accept the existing effect
steps.detail: The next action is ACCEPT_EXISTING_EFFECT; duplicate-effect count remains zero.

unsafe.title: Blind retry
unsafe.decision_note: A missing acknowledgement is treated as failure, and recovery mints a fresh mutation identity.
unsafe.explanation: The original commit state was never resolved, so a new mutation can create an additional financial effect.

steps.title: Submit one intended payment
steps.detail: The first request may already have committed at the provider or ledger boundary.

steps.title: The effect may already exist
steps.detail: A server-side commit can happen before the response reaches the client.

steps.title: The acknowledgement is lost
steps.detail: Local transport uncertainty is incorrectly treated as proof of failure.

steps.title: Retry as a fresh mutation
steps.detail: A new request or effect key no longer represents safe recovery of the same operation.

steps.title: A second effect can be created
steps.detail: Without authoritative resolution, duplicate-effect exposure remains open.
